cards.front: A woman has thin grey discharge with a fishy odour and vaginal pH 5.5. Microscopy shows clue cells and very few of the normally dominant [___].
cards.context:
Bacterial vaginosis is an overgrowth of anaerobes after loss of the acid-producing flora. Clue cells, pH above 4.5 and a fishy amine odour support it.

Current Australian guidance also treats an ongoing male partner, which reduces recurrence.

cards.front: A woman is considering menopausal hormone therapy with her GP and has no personal or family history of venous thrombosis. Before starting, routine [___] screening is not indicated.
cards.context:
Without a personal or family history of venous thromboembolism, a thrombophilia screen does not change the MHT decision.

Thrombotic risk depends on the route of estrogen administration: oral estrogen increases venous thromboembolism risk more than transdermal estrogen.
